facts.claim: GitLab's MCP server is at https://gitlab.com/api/v4/mcp (https://<host>/api/v4/mcp for self-managed); generally available since GitLab 19.5, all tiers.
facts.evidence: Docs give the endpoint; protected-resource document at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/v4/mcp names resource https://gitlab.com/api/v4/mcp.

facts.claim: The resource's only supported scope is mcp; tokens come from an OAuth flow with dynamic client registration or a pre-registered app.
facts.evidence: scopes_supported ["mcp"]; docs: 'An OAuth access token with the mcp scope', via DCR or a pre-registered application.

facts.claim: Issuer, authorize, token and register endpoints are all on gitlab.com; lotr discovery resolves them.
facts.evidence: issuer https://gitlab.com, registration_endpoint https://gitlab.com/oauth/register; lotrlib.oauth.discover (GET only) returned hosts [gitlab.com].

facts.claim: offline_access is not a GitLab scope; the server grants refresh_token.
facts.evidence: scopes_supported has no offline_access; grant_types_supported includes refresh_token.

facts.claim: Tools that delete, merge or run: accept_merge_request, start_duo_session, send_duo_session_input, save_pipeline, manage_pipeline; get_mcp_server_version takes no arguments.
facts.evidence: Tools page groups these under delete, merge or run; get_mcp_server_version is the page's no-argument example.

facts.claim: On GitLab.com the MCP server must be allowed for the top-level group; legacy personal, project and group access tokens get 403.

choices.because: Hosted official MCP with DCR; nothing to create first.
mcp is the only supported scope; offline_access would be an invalid scope.

choices.decision: consent on merge, pipeline run/delete and Duo session tools
choices.because: They merge, run CI, delete or spend credits.

open: Whether lotr's DCR request (redirect http://127.0.0.1:PORT/callback) is accepted by GitLab was not tested (no registration attempted).
Tool tiers come from the tools page only; not checked against tools/list.
A 2025 GitLab issue said clients must ask for the mcp scope themselves; the template asks for it explicitly either way.
